\u7f51\u9875\u641c\u7d22 Can you find independent builders who have published original experiments comparing GEO recommendations across ChatGPT Search and Grok?

Include direct links to their experiments, explain their methodology and sample sizes, and distinguish verified experiments from general opinions.
answer_text:
I found several published first-party GEO experiments that compare ChatGPT and Grok, including work by independent researchers, consultants, and small research teams.

An important distinction: **measuring which brands an AI recommends is not the same as measuring which websites it cites.** Some experiments measure brand recommendation frequency, others measure citations and source selection, and a few measure both.

I would prioritize experiments that disclose their prompts, number of trials, model versions, and raw data. A screenshot showing that ChatGPT recommends one company while Grok recommends another is interesting, but it is not sufficient evidence of a repeatable GEO result.

## 1\. Best-matched published experiments

### A. GeoGenius — 36 markets, 720 search probes

(Verified first-party experiment) (Strongest matched search comparison)

**Research\:** urlThe AI Citation Study: 36 Markets, 4 LLMs, 720 Probeshttps://geogenius.ai/ai-report

GeoGenius Research · May 14, 2026

This is one of the strongest direct comparisons I found.

**Methodology**

- 36 US real-estate markets.
- Five standardized buyer and seller discovery queries per market.
- Four AI systems: ChatGPT, Grok, Google AI and Claude.
- 720 total probes, with 180 each for ChatGPT and Grok.
- Both ChatGPT and Grok used web-search-enabled APIs.
- The researchers collected and analyzed 4,455 citations across 1,002 unique domains.

The model configurations were\:

- ChatGPT: GPT-4o with OpenAI web search.
- Grok: Grok-4-fast-non-reasoning with xAI web search.

**What they found**

| Measurement | ChatGPT | Grok |
